p:cNvPr.descr: An image depicting catabolic pathways for tryptophan, lysine, phenylalanine, tyrosine, leucine, and isoleucine. On the top left is tryptophan in a box. It begins with CH, which bonds up to NH3 (plus sign over N), right to COO- and left to CH2 (all Cs are in blue). CH2 bonds down to the top point of a pentagon. The top right side is double-bonded. The bottom right is N over H. The bottom left side is C. Next to the pentagon is a hexagon which shares a double-bonded side. C is at the bottom, bottom left, and top left points of the hexagon, which has alternating double-bonded sides. The Cs are all in pink. An arrow below this points down and left to alanine, where CH bonds left to CH3, up to NH3 (plus sign over N), and right to COO-. All Cs are blue here. Alanine points down to pyruvate in a blue box. For this, C double bonds up to O, bonds left to CH3 and right to COO-. The Cs are all in blue. On that same arrow, another arrow emerges and points to 2CO2. To the right of the arrow, it states, “9 steps.” The arrow continues down to alpha-ketoadipate. Lysine is to the right and also points down to alpha-ketoadipate. Lysine begins with H3N (plus sign over N) bonds right to CH2, which bonds right to CH2 three more times (where C is pink), then bonds right to CH (C is pink), up to NH3 (plus sign over N) and right to COO-. Alpha-ketoadipate begins with –OOC, which bonds right to CH2, which bonds right to CH2, which bonds right to CH2 (Cs are pink), which bonds right to C (in pink), which double bonds up to O and bonds right to COO-. Below this is an arrow pointing down to glutaryl-CoA. On the left of the arrow, a curved arrow points from CoA-SH to CO2. To the right, NAD+ points to NADH with a curved arrow. Glutaryl-CoA is the same as alpha-ketoadipate, but at the end, the pink C bonds right to S-CoA. From there two arrows point down, then right. The first points to CO2, the second points to acetoacetyl-CoA in a red box. This has 4 steps. Acetoacetyl-CoA begins with C, which bonds left to CH3, double bonds up to O, and bonds right to CH2, which bonds right to C (all Cs are pink). C double bonds up to O and bonds right to S-CoA. At the top right is phenylalanine in a box. It begins with CH (C is pink), which bonds up to NH3 (plus sign over N) and right to COO-. CH also bonds left to CH2 (C is pink), which bonds left to a hexagon with double bonds on the top, bottom left, and bottom right sides. Each point has C. Only the bottom two Cs are pink, all others are blue. An arrow points down from this to tyrosine in a box. This is the same as the phenylalanine, but the left point of the hexagon has C bonding left to HO. An arrow points down from this (5 steps) to acetoacetate. Prior to this, another arrow jets out to the left to fumarate in a blue box. It begins with –OOC, which bonds right to CH, which double bonds right to CH, which bonds right to COO- (all Cs are blue). Acetoacetate begins with C, which double bonds up to O, bonds left to CH3, and right to CH2 (all Cs are pink with a box surrounding them. CH2 also bonds right to COO- (C is pink). To the right, leucine is in a box. It begins with CH, which bonds up and left to H3C and down and left to H3C (all Cs are red and in a box). CH also bonds right to CH2, which bonds right to CH (Cs are blue). CH also bonds up to NH3 (plus sign over N) and right to COO-. Below this is an arrow (6 steps) pointing down, then left to acetyl-CoA. To the right of the arrow is a curved arrow pointing from CoA-SH to CO2. CO2 (C is pink) across the arrow from leucine to acetyl-CoA and points to acetoacetate discussed above. From acetoacetate has an arrow below pointing down, then left to acetoacetyl-CoA. CoA-SH merges into the arrow. The line between leucine and acetyl-CoA states, “fate of blue carbons.” Acetoacetyl-CoA also points down to acetyl-CoA with a straight arrow. CoA-SH is also attached to this arrow. Acetyl-CoA begins with C (in pink), which bond left to CH3 (C is pink), right to S-CoA, and double bonds up to O. To the left of this, an arrow points to acetyl-CoA from isoleucine in a box. This line had a curved arrow on top pointing from 2CoA-SH to CO2 (C is blue). Below the arrow is another arrow jetting down to propionyl-CoA. This begins with CH3 bonding right to CH2, which bonds right to C (all Cs are blue), which double bonds up to O, bond right to S-CoA. Isoleucine begins with CH3, which bonds right to CH2 (Cs are pink), which bonds right to CH, which bonds down to CH3 and right to CH, which bonds up to NH3 (plus sign over N), and right to COO- (these Cs are blue). To the right of propionyl-CoA has an arrow to the right (3 steps) pointing right to succinyl-CoA in a pink box.
